text:
maria: Heads-up — Aperture Analytics signed a Q4 dedicated commit: 10k GPU-hours/month, multi-region (us-west, eu-central, ap-southeast). They want guidance on buffer %, cross-region burst strategy, and cost tradeoffs.
sam: thanks. do we have their traffic shape? steady baseline or big microbursts?
li: their contract appendix shows baseline ~320 rps (inference) steady, with short microbursts up to 2.5x during marketing pushes and APAC morning window. mostly short-lived (5-20m).
jonah: two quick constraints: 1) ap-southeast quotas are tight for guaranteed GPUs in our partner DCs, 2) cross-az networking egress in eu-central adds ~10-15ms and some packet drops we saw last month. both affect burst routing.
priya: recommendation: split commit into "reserved baseline" + "burst pool". reserve ~85% of expected steady GPU-hours in the committed pool, keep a 15% soft buffer for smoothing, and expose a separate burst pool (preemptible/spot) for spikes. For Aperture numbers that is: baseline ~8.5k hours, soft buffer ~1.5k, burst pool target capacity ~3-4k to cover 2.5x spikes for short windows.
maria: math sanity check — if baseline handles steady 320 rps, and peak is 800 rps, what's latency SLO hit if we rely on preemptible burst?
priya: if we warm a small standby warm-pool (~6 GPUs per region) with fast launch time ( <90s) and use prefix caching to reduce KV warm time, the SLO tail can be kept within 2x baseline latency for most spikes. without warm pool, cold launches add ~3-6s tail latency.
sam: cost question: how much $ savings vs full reserved + bigger headroom?
priya: rough calc: fully reserved 12k hours baseline = full cost. Hybrid: reserve 8.5k (committed discount applied) + 3.5k preemptible at ~40% lower unit cost -> ~20-25% savings on total committed bill. exact depends on negotiated discounts and quant profiles.
li: region nuance: for APAC we should keep a slightly bigger warm pool percentageally because quotas + network RTTs make cross-region failover expensive. recommend 20% headroom in ap-southeast (vs 15% elsewhere).
jonah: ops note — we need quota clearances for ap-southeast to guarantee baseline ramps. I'll file a quota request this morning and mark it P0 for the partner DC team.
quota-bot: quota check: current usable GPUs in ap-southeast = 54, requested baseline GPUs for Aperture = 36, recommended warmpool = 8. Potential shortfall = 0 (if partner approval granted).
maria: what about fallback model variants? can we route to a smaller quantized variant automatically on overload?
priya: yes — use policy: prefer same-accuracy model, fallback to q4_int8 variant beyond 95th percentile. That saves ~30-40% GPU time per request and reduces burst demand. We'll include a canary so we monitor quality metrics for Aperture's eval set.
sam: deliverables — priya: draft buffer + burst proposal + rough cost delta by EOD; jonah: quota request + region notes; li: add network risk appendix; maria: coordinate with customer success for expected marketing spikes (dates).
priya: putting draft in #eng-infra-docs — snippet of proposed config: ```
commit_policy:
  baseline_gpus: 36
  buffer_pct: 15
  warm_pool_per_region: 6
  burst_pool: 10 # preemptible
  fallback_variant: q4_int8
```
maria: perfect. if we can also include black-friday simulation (1.8x sustained for 48h) that'll help legal/sales with liability wording.
jonah: noted. I'll run a quick capacity sim after quota request completes.
sam: thanks team — let's sync tomorrow 10am PT after initial numbers. :thumbsup:
